walkthroughs.body_html:
Dickens published A Christmas Carol in December 1843.

He had visited a Ragged School in Field Lane that year and was horrified by the poverty. He originally planned a political pamphlet but decided a story would 'strike a sledgehammer blow' for the poor.

walkthroughs.h2: The Poor Laws and the workhouse
walkthroughs.body_html:
The 1834 Poor Law Amendment Act said relief should only be given inside workhouses — and conditions inside had to be worse than the lowest-paid job outside.

That is why Scrooge snarls 'Are there no prisons? Are there no workhouses?' His view was the official Victorian view.

Thomas Malthus argued the poor would breed faster than food could grow, so charity made things worse.

Scrooge echoes him: 'they had better do it, and decrease the surplus population.' Dickens makes the Ghost of Christmas Present throw these words back at Scrooge in Stave 3.
